description: We are a team passionate about combining science, technology, music, and accessibility. Our project, EarthEcho, transforms NASA's Earth observation data into interactive visual and audio experiences, helping people understand environmental changes through sound. We are interested in creating an accessible platform for everyone, including visually impaired users. We welcome teammates with skills in web development, data science, audio engineering, UI/UX design, and research.
summary:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive web-based experience that transforms NASA Earth science visualizations into sound through sonification.

The project currently features two environmental tracks: Ocean Symphony, which explores global ocean currents and temperature patterns, and Air Quality: PM2.5, an experimental extension that explores air-quality data through sound.

Users can select dated visualization frames, explore a 10 × 8 map grid, listen to individual data cells, navigate across the map, and hear audio overviews. Data patterns are translated into sound, offering an alternative way to experience environmental information beyond conventional visualizations.

Earth Jukebox aims to make Earth science more engaging, exploratory, and accessible, particularly for blind and low-vision audiences. By combining NASA data, interactive technology, and creative sonification, the project demonstrates how listening can become another way to understand our changing planet.
details:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive web application designed to transform NASA Earth science visualizations into an auditory experience through sonification.

The main experience, Ocean Symphony, uses NASA's Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature visualization (SVS 3912). The visualization is divided into a 10 × 8 grid, allowing users to explore individual cells and hear sounds representing the underlying visual data. Users can select different dated frames, navigate across the map, listen to individual cells, and play audio overviews.

The project also includes Air Quality: PM2.5, an experimental track based on NASA's particulate matter visualization (SVS 5151). It explores the potential of translating atmospheric pollution patterns into sound.

The project combines interactive web technologies, data interpretation, and audio synthesis to create an alternative approach to science communication. Its design considers accessibility, including opportunities for blind and low-vision users to experience environmental information through listening.

Our creative approach focuses on making scientific exploration interactive rather than simply presenting static visualizations. We aim to demonstrate that sound can complement visual information and help people engage with the complexity of Earth's changing environment.

Technology Stack

Earth Jukebox was developed using React and TypeScript, with Vite as the development and build tool. For audio generation, the project uses the native Web Audio API, allowing soundscapes to be generated and controlled directly in the browser without relying on external audio or state management libraries.

Claude (Anthropic) was used as an AI assistance tool during the development process.
